_about: Seeded tracker details for the request screens (Authorizations, Sent, Info request, Partials, Early discharge, Peer-to-peer). Synthetic. Keyed by request id; 'fill' supplies tracker fields the seed row lacks (the live row always wins).

R-0391.next: Expect "why were units used early?" — justification attached.

info.asked: Please provide additional clinical information to support the level of care requested: (1) frequency and amount of alcohol and other substance use in the last 30 days, with any urine drug screen or breath alcohol results; (2) withdrawal history and current withdrawal risk; (3) prior treatment at a lower level of care and its outcome; (4) current living situation and recovery supports; (5) current ASAM dimensional ratings and the level of care requested.
items: Frequency and amount of use in the last 30 days, with any screen results
Withdrawal history and current withdrawal risk
Prior treatment at a lower level of care and its outcome
Current living situation and recovery supports
Current ASAM dimensional ratings and the level of care requested
answers: At the screening call on October 9 the family reported that K.T. drank on 7 of the previous 30 days (September 9 to October 8), five to eight drinks each time<sup>1</sup>. Two attempts to stop in that period each lasted under a week<sup>2</sup>. No urine drug screen or breath alcohol result is on file yet<sup>1</sup>.

K.T. had tremor and nausea after a weekend binge in August and needed no medication<sup>2</sup>. Her last drink was October 4 and she has had no withdrawal symptoms in the last 30 days<sup>2</sup>. The October 9 assessment rates withdrawal potential 2 (Moderate)<sup>2</sup>.

K.T. attended weekly outpatient counseling at Piedmont Counseling (Level 1) from January to April 2026, nine sessions<sup>3</sup>. Treatment ended when the family lost transportation. Drinking episodes did not decrease during or after that period (four in March, five in April)<sup>3</sup>.

K.T. lives with her father and stepmother; alcohol is kept unlocked in the home<sup>4</sup>. An aunt who lives nearby has offered rides<sup>4</sup>. She was referred through juvenile court diversion and said at intake she is not sure drinking is a problem<sup>5</sup>.

Ratings on October 9<sup>2</sup>: withdrawal potential 2, medical conditions 1, emotional and behavioral 1, readiness to change 3, relapse and continued use 3, recovery environment 2. The clinician recommended Level 2.1 (intensive outpatient), the level requested<sup>2</sup>. The ratings and the recommendation are the clinician's.
sources: Piedmont Counseling discharge letter (family link upload)

brief.open_with: "This is Jordan Perez, LPC, license and NPI on the request. I'm calling about a 16-year-old girl in our Campbell County intensive outpatient program who was approved for 65 of the 150 units we requested."

criteria.title: Relapse and continued use (D5).
criteria.text: Non-prescribed stimulant use reported Oct 10 and Oct 20, positive urine screens Oct 16 and Oct 25: 4 dated episodes in 16 days, after 3 episodes in the 14 days before intake. Rated 3 (Significant) on Oct 1.

criteria.title: Recovery environment (D6).
criteria.text: Shares a bedroom with a cousin who sells pills; her mother works two jobs and is out until 9 pm most evenings. Rated 3 (Significant).

criteria.title: Emotional and behavioral conditions (D3).
criteria.text: PHQ-9 17 on Oct 22 (18 at intake); passive thoughts of death, no plan; safety plan updated Oct 22. Rated 3 (Significant).

criteria.title: Treatment that has not worked.
criteria.text: Weekly counseling with the referral partner's counselor since Sept 2025, ongoing, no change in use. Outpatient counseling Jan–May 2026, 11 sessions, ended by the provider as "not making progress".

brief.level_of_care: The Oct 1 assessment recommended Level 2.5 (partial hospitalization) and the psychiatrist raised it again on Oct 26. Level 2.1 is requested because the family cannot provide rides for 20 hours a week. With fewer than the 150 units requested she is without a daily structured program: she used all 65 by Oct 28 and is still in service, unpaid.
questions: Weekly counseling since Sept 2025 and 11 outpatient sessions from Jan to May 2026 did not change her use; the provider ended that treatment as "not making progress". D3, D5 and D6 are each rated 3 (Significant).

She has passive thoughts of death and no plan (PHQ-9 17 on Oct 22); the safety plan was updated Oct 22 and the psychiatrist saw her Oct 26. The request rests on the dimension ratings and the level recommendation, not on suicide risk alone.
The clinician's own recommendation was Level 2.5; Level 2.1 is the step the family can attend. Staff log start and stop times on their phones for every group (3 units a day). I can send the log.

Outpatient counseling ended in May 2026 without change; intensive outpatient began Oct 5. Four use episodes in the last 16 days (Oct 10, 16, 20 and 25). The goal is 4 of 5 weekly screens negative before step-down.

R-0384.denial_text: Only the family member can appeal. Drafted for the family: a one-page plain-language letter, the reason restated ("already connected to other services" and "Level 1 outpatient is appropriate"), and what the payer's own letter means, so "approved for less" is not read as "no longer at risk." Harvest keeps serving in the meantime; that choice is logged with the date.

payer_history.sent: More evidence (use episodes, a positive screen, leaving group early) + counter at 140
payer_history.lesson: below the opening offer. More information produced a smaller award.

denial_reasons.check: Pulls the six stored ASAM ratings with the clinician's note and date for each; D4, D5 and D6 come with their dated records from the last 30 days (attendance counts, use episodes and screens, home environment), and the dimensions above what Level 1 can manage are named.

denial_reasons.reason: "Can be managed at a lower level of care (outpatient)"
denial_reasons.check: Prior-treatment table (level, provider, dates, outcome) from earlier outpatient care, plus D5 use episodes and screens from the last 30 days and the home environment record; "information about outpatient" and pro-bono contacts are flagged as not counting as prior care.

Current-services table states each service's frequency and why it is not enough alone; weekly counseling with a referral partner is listed under care coordination, next to the dated D5 use record and D6 home environment that show its effect.
D1 rating and note, the withdrawal screen (CIWA or COWS), last-use date and any withdrawal history, pulled as dated records from the last 30 days.
PHQ-9 or GAD-7 scores with dates, safety-plan reviews and the co-occurring diagnosis and its treatment (D3) from the last 30 days; the draft blocks when a rating of 2 or more has no instrument score.

Date of the latest ASAM assessment against the reassessment rule (30 days in the demo rules table); an overdue reassessment, or one indicated by an incident since the last assessment, is flagged before the request goes out.

denial_reasons.reason: "No documented use in the last 30 days"
denial_reasons.check: Dated use episodes, urine drug screens and craving ratings inside the last 30 days (D5); older facts are listed with their date and not counted as current.
Home and living environment record with its date (who in the home uses, supports, transport) (D6); household disclosures stay out unless the clinician presses Include.
Attendance counts from the group notes (attended of scheduled), the client's own stated goal and stage of change (D4); counts, never percentages.
